title: Kitesurf is now open source
description: Kitesurf, our experimental browser engine for AI agents, is now open source. Inspect the code, run it locally, or deploy your own instance on Cloudflare Workers.

title: Adapting to AI penetration testing orchestrators: The Modern Security Model
description: AI-orchestrated penetration testing platforms like ARTEX have become increasingly powerful tools enabling effective attacks on exposed infrastructure. Here we share Cloudflare’s observations and recommended countermeasures.

title: Global Domain Activity Trends Seen in Q3 2026
description: Global new domain registrations rose 16.8% to more than 35.1 million in Q3 2026, while WhoisXML API identified over 8.2 million potentially malicious registrations and reported shifts in leading TLDs and DNS activity.

title: Introducing Spend Management: Spending limits and alerts for Cloudflare
description: Spend Management adds opt-in spending caps for Cloudflare Workers and Durable Objects, and more products soon. Here is how we built the metering pipeline that turns usage into runtime decisions.

title: Could pigeons deliver the Internet?
description: Guest Post: What happens when we replace network cables with carrier pigeons? We worked out how many birds you would need.

title: Post-Quantum Authentication: Lessons from Prague
description: In October, the Internet Architecture Board (IAB) held a two-day workshop in Prague with people who are deploying post-quantum authentication. These are the first impressions from the co-chairs, ahead of the full workshop report.

title: Capture Before the Letter: What Recent UDRP Decisions Say About Website Evidence
description: An analysis of 301 WIPO domain disputes finds substantial gaps in Internet Archive coverage, highlighting why preserving dated website evidence before notifying registrants can be critical to establishing bad faith in UDRP proceedings.

title: Iranian Websites Lose .com Domains as GoDaddy Registrar Holds Emerge
description: Iranian websites face domain disruptions linked to GoDaddy registrar holds, prompting migrations to .ir addresses. Registration records identify affected domains, but the legal basis and scope of the restrictions remain unclear.

title: ARIN Online Achieves SOC 2 Compliance
description: ARIN has successfully completed an initial Service Organizational Control (SOC) 2 Type II audit of ARIN Online and renewed compliance for our Resource Public Key Infrastructure (RPKI) for the fourth year.

title: 2026 APNIC Survey: Executive Council Response
description: The 2026 APNIC Survey highlights strong confidence in APNIC’s services and the priorities of Members and stakeholders across the region.

title: [Podcast] Submarine cable resilience and economics
description: How resilient is the global submarine cable network? Geoff Huston explores its evolution, vulnerabilities, economics, and who has an interest in keeping it running.

title: What’s up with email at IETF 127
description: Email is the oldest widely used application on the Internet, but it continues to evolve. At IETF 127 four working groups will meet to improve the security and usability of mail, and two Birds-of-a-Feather sessions propose improvements in mail operations and the way users sign up …

title: Choosing QuePaxa, an unusual consensus algorithm
description: Cloudflare is building an experimental consensus service using a never-before-deployed consensus algorithm, QuePaxa. In this post we explain how QuePaxa works and why we chose it.

title: Verisign Reverses Plan to Eliminate Existing .name Domains and Email Services
description: Verisign has withdrawn plans to terminate existing third-level .name domains and email-forwarding services following registrant objections. Existing registrations will remain supported while at least one accredited registrar continues offering the services.

title: SIDN publishes RSSAC002 traffic metrics for .nl
description: Guest Post: SIDN Labs shares insight into traffic to the authoritative .nl nameservers.

title: What a Decade of DNS Query Data Tells Us About the Next Algorithm Transition
description: Monthly ICANN activity reports from top-level domain registries provide a rare, consistent, long-term view of DNS query traffic across registries, offering publicly available, operator-reported data on query volumes over UDP and TCP.

title: Every Agent Needs a Name, and the Domain Industry Would Like to Sell It
description: Competing DNS-based proposals seek to establish verifiable identities for AI agents, raising questions about accountability, interoperability, and the commercial interests of domain industry players positioning themselves to shape the emerging infrastructure for agent identity.

title: The Hilco Global IPv4.Global Practice Releases ProVision 9.0, Expanding Network Management, Automation and Administrative Control
description: Hilco Global's IPv4.Global practice has released ProVision 9.0, introducing enhanced IP address management, DNS and DHCP administration, peering automation and security controls to help organizations manage increasingly complex network infrastructure.

title: ICANN’s Community TLD Policy Faces Renewed Scrutiny as 2026 gTLD Round Advances
description: BRS Media is urging ICANN to assess whether community domains approved in the 2012 new gTLD round have served their intended communities, as concerns over preferential treatment resurface in the 2026 application round.

title: Earth Sirrush Espionage Tool Evolution: DNS Facts Unveiled
description: A DNS investigation into the Russia-aligned Earth Sirrush espionage campaign identifies potentially malicious domains, historical infrastructure connections and 95 IP addresses belonging to possible victims of attacks targeting Ukrainian government, defense and logistics organiza…

title: October 2026 IPv4 Market Report: Broad-Based Price Gains Extend Recovery as Large-Block Discounts Narrow
description: IPv4 prices rose across all major allocation categories in October as transaction volumes remained steady. Large-block prices continued their recovery, narrowing historical discounts and highlighting changing acquisition economics ahead of year-end.

title: The Machine Majority: What Bot Traffic Looks Like from Central Asia
description: Most web pages are now fetched by machines rather than people, at least on the networks we can measure. I pulled data for thirteen countries across Central Asia and the Caucasus to see what that looks like from our corner of the world, and what it means for those of us who run ne…

title: IETF Administration LLC 2027 Draft Budget
description: The IETF Administration LLC has prepared its draft budget for 2027 and now seeks community feedback.

title: Launching the Vite Ecosystem Fund
description: Cloudflare is distributing the first $301,300 of the Vite Ecosystem Fund to open source projects and maintainers. The recipients were chosen by a panel of Vite stack core team members, including maintainers not employed by Cloudflare.

title: Your Router Trusts Its Validator. But Who's Watching the Validator?
description: ROV turned your validator into a forwarding policy source. The registries have strengthened their side of the RPKI, but the chain from repository to router runs on your infrastructure. When that chain breaks, it often breaks silently.

title: The DOs and don’ts of post-quantum DNSSEC
description: Post-quantum signatures could dramatically enlarge DNSSEC responses, shifting many queries from UDP to TCP. Should resolvers limit unnecessary DNSSEC data, or is greater TCP use inevitable?

title: The post-quantum future of web privacy
description: Cryptographic protocols like Privacy Pass help keep web sites safe from abuse while keeping their users private. This post looks at the quantum threat to these protocols, and some new post-quantum cryptography that may help close the gap.

title: The Internet's New Factories
description: AI factories create several traffic systems at once, and power is shaping where they can be built. This article asks what operators can see, what stays private, and who decides how these systems are connected.

title: PCAP-LM: Helping AI assistants read network traffic
description: Guest Post: Packet captures are the ground truth of network operations, but analysing them is slow, requires specialist expertise, and does not scale. PCAP-LM rewrites captures into a form that AI assistants can read, helping address that mismatch.

title: Agents aren’t humans (but they kinda are)
description: AI agents act for millions, but servers see intermediaries that strip user visibility. This post defines the problem space and introduces a collaborative approach to safely identifying, allowing, and managing this automated traffic.

title: Do Registrars Use DNSSEC on Their Own Domains?
description: Registrars must support DNSSEC for customers, but how many use it themselves? A study of 698 registrar domains finds fewer than one in ten has a DS record, with European registrars ahead of the rest. Tobias Sattler explores the gap and its possible explanations.

title: The Internet didn’t break; we just forgot what it was leaning on
description: Guest Post: When international links fail, hidden dependencies can take local services with them. Here’s how operators can design for local resilience.

title: See the agents, set the terms: New visibility and control for personal agents
description: Personal AI agents have changed how users interact with the web, blurring the lines between automated and human traffic. Learn how Cloudflare gives site owners visibility and control to manage personal agent access.

title: The RIPE Chair Team Reports - Highlights from RIPE 93
description: From digital independence and practical AI to inclusion and research, RIPE 93 gave the community plenty to discuss and act on. The RIPE Chair Team shares personal highlights from Sofia and ways to get involved in the work ahead.

title: Solar PV for Internet resilience (Part 1): Designing your system
description: Guest Post: Solar photovoltaics and battery storage can provide reliable power for network infrastructure, even in remote locations. Here’s what’s good to know before selecting equipment.

title: Introducing Zero Wire, a hub for investigating critical Internet vulnerabilities
description: Zero Wire on Cloudflare Radar pairs plain-language briefings with global attack telemetry and remediation steps. Triage critical CVEs faster and decide how to protect your infrastructure.

title: Restating the case for DNSSEC
description: Does TLS make DNSSEC unnecessary? An examination of common DNSSEC assumptions challenges that argument and considers DNSSEC's role in establishing trust, the risks of partial deployment, and the evidence from real-world outages.

title: How we halved DNS build delay and cut memory use by 85%
description: Zone setting changes used to rebuild entire DNS zones, even ones with tens of millions of records. Here is how we built a planner that picks the smallest safe build, cutting full builds by 40%, peak memory by 85%, and halving build delay.
